source.title: Adaptively Preconditioned Stochastic Gradient Langevin Dynamics

record.tranche_reason: Compares an adaptive preconditioned SGLD optimizer with SGD and adaptive optimizers on CIFAR-10 and reports held-out accuracy/generalization outcomes.
record.gate_note: The study reports optimizer comparisons and training/test accuracy plots. It does not test random-label memorization, width scaling, architecture bias, dropout, sharpness measures, or memorized-example removal. Plot values are not tabulated numerically.
record.test_reason: The experiments include SGD with momentum, Adam, AdaGrad and AMSGrad on CIFAR-10 under learning-rate tuning. Their held-out comparisons bear on V4, although the extracted rows record only comparisons against the proposed ASGLD method.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors claim ASGLD combines adaptive methods' convergence speed with SGD-like or better generalization, improves stability relative to SGD, and becomes more effective in deeper networks.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces adaptively preconditioned stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics and compares it with SGD and first-order adaptive methods; does not reproduce the optimizer comparisons in the cited studies.
record.method_sensitivity: The narrative describes the adaptive-method generalization advantage as emerging by the time the learning rate is decayed; performance is shown over the 200-epoch schedule with decay at epoch 150.

fits_no_version.finding: ASGLD matches SGD's held-out accuracy on ResNet-34, exceeds it on DenseNet-121, and reportedly outperforms conventional adaptive optimizers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive noise preconditioning in SGLD can combine competitive held-out accuracy with fast convergence on these CIFAR-10 architectures.

record.peer_reviewed: ICML 2019 Workshop on Understanding and Improving Generalization in Deep Learning
record.problems: Results are limited to CIFAR-10 with two architectures and a fixed 200-epoch schedule. Accuracy values and uncertainty estimates are not stated in the text; plotted results are not tabulated.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and corresponding natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
Width scaling beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the role of local connectivity.

Language benchmarks, broader hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching optimizers, and equal or better adaptive-optimizer training performance. The supplied figures expose test-accuracy axes but no readable training-performance results.
Batch-size interventions and adaptations to large-batch training.
Dropout interventions and interactions with training-set size or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness measurements and their ranking of generalization gaps.

missing.what: Direct SGD-with-momentum versus Adam, AdaGrad and AMSGrad held-out comparisons for ResNet-34. The narrative indirectly supports SGD's advantage, but the record contains only ASGLD comparisons.

Direct SGD-with-momentum versus each conventional adaptive optimizer on DenseNet-121. Their ordering cannot be established from ASGLD outperforming both groups; curve values are unavailable in the supplied text.

record.verdict_notes: Learning rates were tuned on an expandable five-point logarithmic grid; batch size, weight decay and dropout followed the base architectures. No numerical accuracy differences or uncertainty estimates are readable here. The authors' use of significance language does not establish a statistical significance test. DenseNet's direct SGD-versus-adaptive ordering remains unresolved.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and generalization on natural labels.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison.
The reported comparison is on CIFAR-10 image classifiers; broader language benchmarks and broader hyperparameter tuning are not tested.
Large versus small batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout intervention and its interaction with data augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to generalization gap.
Removal and retraining of memorized examples.

rows.subject: Resnet 34
rows.operation_detail: Compared ASGLD with SGD with momentum during CIFAR-10 training.
rows.measure: Test accuracy on held-out set / generalization error
rows.baseline: SGD (with momentum); numerical value not stated
rows.value: ASGLD achieves similar accuracy on the held out set; numerical value not stated
rows.note: Authors describe held-out accuracy as similar; no numerical values are provided.
rows.check: Records the proposed method's performance against SGD, rather than conventional adaptive optimizers against SGD. Similar ASGLD and SGD accuracy does not itself establish absence of V4's effect.

rows.subject: Resnet 34
rows.operation_detail: Compared ASGLD with first-order adaptive methods during CIFAR-10 training.
rows.baseline: AdaGrad, Adam, AMSGrad; numerical values not stated
rows.value: ASGLD significantly outperforms adaptive methods in generalization error by the time learning rates are decayed; numerical value not stated
rows.note: Text states ASGLD has similar training speed to adaptive methods early, then significantly outperforms them in generalization error by the learning-rate decay.
rows.check: Records ASGLD outperforming adaptive optimizers, not SGD outperforming them. This method-performance comparison should be replaced by the relevant baseline-optimizer comparison.

rows.subject: Densenet 121
rows.operation_detail: Compared ASGLD with SGD with momentum during CIFAR-10 training.
rows.measure: Test accuracy on held-out set / generalization error
rows.baseline: SGD (with momentum); numerical value not stated
rows.value: ASGLD has a lower generalization error than SGD at the end of training; numerical value not stated
rows.note: The reported advantage is at the end of training; figures provide no tabulated numerical values.
rows.check: ASGLD outperforming SGD does not measure whether conventional adaptive optimizers generalize worse than SGD. The assigned partial state is unsupported for V4.

rows.subject: Densenet 121
rows.operation_detail: Compared ASGLD with first-order adaptive methods during CIFAR-10 training.
rows.baseline: AdaGrad, Adam, AMSGrad; numerical values not stated
rows.value: The paper says ASGLD significantly outperforms first-order adaptive methods in generalization; numerical value not stated
rows.note: The explicit detailed comparison by adaptive optimizer is plotted; the narrative's broad generalization conclusion is not accompanied by numeric values.
rows.check: ASGLD outperforming adaptive optimizers does not establish their ordering relative to SGD, especially because ASGLD also outperforms SGD on DenseNet.

relationships.condition: ResNet-34 on CIFAR-10, late in the 200-epoch schedule with learning-rate decay at epoch 150 and learning-rate grid tuning.
relationships.reason: Based on Section 4 text rather than a captured direct-comparison row: ASGLD approximately matches SGD while outperforming Adam, AdaGrad and AMSGrad late in training, indirectly supporting worse held-out performance for those adaptive optimizers.
relationships.display_finding: ASGLD reportedly approximately matched SGD while surpassing Adam, AdaGrad, and AMSGrad late in training, but this indirect comparison remains unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Resnet 34 and Densenet 121 on CIFAR-10, with the stated 200-epoch schedule
reader_labels.reason: ASGLD is reported to achieve similar held-out accuracy to SGD on Resnet 34 and lower generalization error than SGD on Densenet 121, while significantly outperforming the adaptive methods by learning-rate decay (R1–R4).
